subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was fired and handed a confession, a heart, and a cleaver he could not crack, but later devised a patient academic strategy to remove Bookwyrm from power without direct confrontation.
source_quote: Kalan Strongbranch didn't want to twist Bookwyrm's arm, in case she escapes it and ends up being his boss.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is suspected of hiding a crime by placing a heart in the chalice of a statue to protect Alkrist, and faces potential removal from her position at Candlekeep due to suspicion and academic protocol.
source_quote: She didn't commit one — but she hid a crime.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist confessed under Kalan's Zone of Truth spell to killing Janussi, and is believed to have murdered his nephew, with Bookwyrm covering for him.
source_quote: Alkrist had confessed. Kalan Strongbranch hadn't yet come back into the room, and we knew there was a thread running from all this back to A'lai.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin pushed for direct action against Bookwyrm and sought a magical book to prove her guilt, ultimately accepting Kalan’s strategy of using the reward to obtain evidence after the fact.
source_quote: There's got to be a book somewhere in the library we can use to actually get to the bottom of this.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir obsessively analyzed wording and protocol, insisting on academic precision and questioning whether Kalan’s strategy was moral or merely cynical.
source_quote: But from your own perspective — isn't that immoral? We're effectively preventing Bookwyrm, if innocent, from serving this role.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz provided the fallback contingency of 'hacking and slashing' whenever the group’s plans became too abstract or risky.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is the site of a naming ceremony for the new head of the Avowed, where suspicion, academic protocol, and power politics determine the fate of Bookwyrm.
source_quote: Tomorrow morning's naming ceremony clearly will not name her.

subject: chalice of the statue
fact: The chalice of the statue contained the heart of Janussi, placed there by Bookwyrm to conceal the murder, and became the central physical clue in the investigation.
source_quote: She put the heart into the chalice of the statue.

subject: Zone of Truth spell
fact: The Zone of Truth spell is not a lock but a pressure — it cannot force truth, only reveal whether the subject can resist it, and its use has evolved from covert casting to public demand.
source_quote: It isn't a lock, it's a pressure.

subject: Kalan's paper
fact: Kalan's paper established that a confession alone is insufficient for truth — three different kinds of evidence are required — a standard now used to shield Bookwyrm from conviction.
source_quote: The confession is one spell — the weakest channel, by the standard I wrote.

subject: cleaver
fact: The cleaver was found alongside the heart and confession, proving someone had covered up the crime cleverly, but did not identify the perpetrator.
source_quote: The heart and the cleaver prove someone covered this up cleverly.

subject: heart of Janussi
fact: The heart of Janussi was removed from his body and placed in the chalice of the statue, becoming the key physical artifact of the cover-up.
source_quote: Alkrist killed him, right? And she's trying to protect Alkrist.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is an infamous group that precedes the party in rumors, larger and more menacing, and has been falsely linked to their crimes in underground posters.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard has a legend now that walks a tunnel ahead of us, and it lies about our height.

subject: Avowed
fact: The Avowed are the governing body of Candlekeep, whose members will vote on Bookwyrm’s fate during the naming ceremony, influenced by suspicion and academic protocol rather than direct evidence.
source_quote: The new head may give Bookwyrm one of two choices: continue as a member of the Avowed, or submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: naming ceremony
fact: The naming ceremony will determine the next head of the Avowed at Candlekeep, and is expected to exclude Bookwyrm and A'lai due to suspicion, paving the way for Fembris Lancer.
source_quote: Tomorrow morning's naming ceremony clearly will not name her.

subject: Alkrist's confession
fact: Alkrist's confession under the Zone of Truth spell provided the first concrete breakthrough in the case, but lacked corroborating evidence to identify the mastermind behind the murder.
source_quote: Alkrist had said it out loud, in the room, with Kalan's spell still holding him honest — he'd killed Janussi.

subject: Kalan's shift to patient strategy
fact: Kalan abandoned direct confrontation and instead planned to wait for Bookwyrm’s political isolation, then use the reward to obtain a magical book that would prove her culpability after the fact.
source_quote: If you do it after the fact, that's much better.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is referenced as a place where similar academic manipulations occurred, with the same pattern of using suspicion to destroy a target without direct accusation.
source_quote: I have seen this move before, in Gracklstugh, dressed in different robes.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was the murdered sage whose heart was removed and hidden, and whose death triggered the investigation and academic debate over truth, evidence, and justice.
source_quote: And the person who declined it is dead." "Janussi.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is the anticipated successor to Bookwyrm as head of the Avowed, elected by default due to the collapse of Bookwyrm’s credibility.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer will probably get elected the new avowed.

subject: book to prove culpability
fact: Kalan will research and provide a magical book that can prove Bookwyrm’s guilt after the naming ceremony, using the reward as leverage to access it from the new head of Candlekeep.
source_quote: I will come up with such a book before you leave.

subject: Kalan's offer to give full report to Bookwyrm
fact: Kalan offered to give Bookwyrm a full report of the evidence against her, to pressure her into declining the position — thus implying guilt without direct accusation.
source_quote: I will give it to Bookwyrm herself.

subject: Dawnbringer's psychic communication
fact: Dawnbringer communicated telepathically with the narrator, expressing a need for further therapy sessions after a productive first session, and the narrator acknowledged her as 'she' despite uncertainty.
source_quote: *I'm not leaving here without the therapy. That first session was actually very productive.*

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a telepathic entity who has been hunting a sword whisperer since the road south, and now seeks further therapeutic sessions to understand the psychological toll of the search.
source_quote: I'd been the one hunting a sword whisperer for her since the road south — months where the thing she was built to carry just wasn't there.

subject: Zalthir's question about the confession's wording
fact: Zalthir questioned whether Kalan’s phrasing — 'you have a confession, a heart, and a cleaver' — implied that the confession was not discounted, despite its insufficiency under academic standards.
source_quote: He said: you have a confession. A heart and a cleaver.

subject: Kalan's refusal to sneak
fact: Kalan refused to cast the Zone of Truth spell covertly again, insisting on a public, bold demand for submission — a shift motivated by fear of future consequences rather than principle.
source_quote: I will not sneak this time. We will walk in, and we will boldly demand that she submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: A'lai
fact: A'lai is a potential candidate for the new head of the Avowed, but is also suspected of being entangled in the case, and will not be named due to the surrounding suspicion.
source_quote: A'lai won't be named either.

subject: chalice of the statue
fact: The chalice of the statue was the container for the heart of Janussi, hidden as part of a cover-up orchestrated by Bookwyrm to protect Alkrist.
source_quote: She put the heart into the chalice of the statue.

subject: confession
fact: The confession from Alkrist, compelled by the Zone of Truth spell, was the only direct evidence in the case, but deemed insufficient by academic standards requiring three distinct forms of proof.
source_quote: The confession is one spell — the weakest channel, by the standard I wrote.

subject: the click in the narrator's skull
fact: A psychic click, likened to a palm slapping stone, occurred in the narrator’s mind during Dawnbringer’s telepathic communication, signaling an unexplained but impactful moment of connection.
source_quote: a click inside my skull, a sound like a palm slapping stone

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who marked in the margin that the group had come all this way to convict a woman not of murder but of embarrassment, and that everyone in the room seemed content with the trade.
source_quote: I only took notes and marked, in the margin, that we had come all this way to convict a woman not of murder but of embarrassment, and that everyone in the room seemed content with the trade.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by himself as the one who said, 'Never miss an opportunity to grift, man,' after Glabbagool stole the potion of flying.
source_quote: Never miss an opportunity to grift, man,

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by Bookwyrm as one of the heroic adventurers whose names escape her, alongside others including Grygum and Daz.
source_quote: I can assure the heroic adventurers — whose names escape me, yes, yes, Zalthir, and so on — that tomorrow morning you will all be given ample opportunity to express your convictions about what may or may not have happened.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is referenced by himself as the one who offered '118' as a taster protocol for the food, meaning nothing to Fembris and everything to the group.
source_quote: I'd say 118,

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is referenced by Bookwyrm as the one who was asked to take his position once more as head of the Avowed, and who promised a full report tomorrow.
source_quote: Would you be so willing as to take your position once more? ... But this will not change the nature of my report tomorrow.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is referenced by herself as the one who drank tea while watching the adventurers over the rim, and who claimed that tea was good for soothing the nerves after talk of murder.
source_quote: And she drank some, watching us over the rim. ... With all this talk of murder in the house, I think a little tea is good for soothing the nerves.

subject: Bookwyrm's office
fact: Bookwyrm's office was arranged the way a room gets arranged when someone wants you to understand the seating before you sit, and the tea was already poured.
source_quote: Her office was arranged the way a room gets arranged when someone wants you to understand the seating before you sit. The tea was already poured.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum was filled with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, tables, and the dry smell of old paper, and served as a guarded waiting room for the adventurers.
source_quote: They put us in Deneir's office to wait out the evening. Bookshelves floor to ceiling, tables, the dry smell of old paper — a room built for people who read for a living, now doing duty as a cell.

subject: Alkrist's safe
fact: Alkrist's safe contained a potion of flying, a potion of superior healing, a fat purse of gold coins, and one red herring-stamped coin.
source_quote: A potion of flying. A potion of superior healing. A fat purse of gold coins, more than a man keeps for honest reasons. And one coin that did not match the rest. ... One of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red.

subject: potion of flying
fact: The potion of flying was stolen by Glabbagool's arm from Alkrist's safe while everyone was distracted, and carried away without notice.
source_quote: While she's talking, my Glabbagool arm swipes the potion of flying. ... Glabbagool's arm came out low and quiet, the way I'd have wanted it if I'd trained him for it, which I had not, not yet. It closed around the vial, drew it back, and no one turned.

subject: red herring coin
fact: The red herring coin was one of the gold coins in Alkrist's safe, stamped with a red herring, and served as a deceptive but harmless detail.
source_quote: One of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is referenced by Grygum as the ooze fused along his forearm that consumed tea and later the potion of flying, and who internally expressed approval of the flying skill.
source_quote: Glabbagool was pleased with himself. *I like the flying skill,* he offered. *That was a good skill.*

subject: sapphire
fact: A sapphire was sought by Grygum using a Locate Object spell, but was not found on Bookwyrm.
source_quote: I wanted to know if she had one on her — that would have been interesting. The spell went out and found nothing. She did not have it.

subject: theft of the potion of flying
fact: The potion of flying was stolen from Alkrist's safe by Glabbagool's arm while the room was distracted, and no one noticed the theft.
source_quote: Glabbagool's arm came out low and quiet... It closed around the vial, drew it back, and no one turned. Not one head.

subject: the food tasting protocol
fact: The group established a taster protocol using Fembris Lancer, assigning him the role of '118' to consume food before the others, and he survived without incident.
source_quote: I'd say 118," ... "Fembris ate on, blessedly unaware that he had just been promoted.

subject: the revelation of Bookwyrm's relief
fact: Bookwyrm's tears and heartbreak over Alkrist's betrayal were observed by Grygum and Daz to be performative, masking genuine relief that the blame had shifted.
source_quote: The tears were correct and the eyes behind them were doing something else. Daz caught it too — I saw him go quiet and still, the way he does when he's found the seam in a thing. She was not sad. She was relieved.

subject: the closing of Alkrist's safe
fact: The safe was closed with all contents inside — including the potion of flying — and declared of no interest, despite the potion having been stolen moments before.
source_quote: They closed the safe with everything still inside — the gold, the herring, the healing — and declared it of no interest.

subject: the appointment of Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Bookwyrm reinstated Kalan Strongbranch as head of the Avowed, acknowledging his methodology had proven its merit, despite his prior removal.
source_quote: Well, it would seem, Kalan, that your methodology has proven its merit. Well done. ... Would you be so willing as to take your position once more?

subject: the escort to Deneir's Sanctum
fact: The adventurers were escorted to Deneir's Sanctum under the pretense of protection, but in reality to isolate them from further investigation.
source_quote: I'm simply doing this to protect you. As you so correctly pointed out, there are other criminal elements within the society, and I would hate for something terrible to happen to you.

subject: Alkrist's prison cell
fact: Alkrist was held secure in the prisons, under guard, following his confession and implication of Bookwyrm.
source_quote: Alkrist will spend the day in the prisons, where he'll be kept secure and unable to escape.

subject: potion of superior healing
fact: The potion of superior healing was one of the items found in Alkrist's safe, alongside the potion of flying and gold coins.
source_quote: A potion of flying. A potion of superior healing. A fat purse of gold coins...

subject: fat purse of gold coins
fact: The fat purse of gold coins found in Alkrist's safe contained more than a man keeps for honest reasons, suggesting illicit gain.
source_quote: A fat purse of gold coins, more than a man keeps for honest reasons.

subject: the request to cure Daral
fact: Daral asked the group whether they would cure him of his condition, revealing his fear of being left broken and unworthy of the spell.
source_quote: Are you guys going to cure me or anything?" ... "under the scholarship, the small fear of being left broken because we'd decided he wasn't worth the spell.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is referenced by Grygum as the one who sat silently during arguments and later served as the group's food taster, eating without suspicion.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer had stood off to one side the whole time we argued, saying nothing, which I respected. ... Fembris, on the other hand, had no such reservations — come, come, come, already reaching, all appetite and no suspicion.

subject: the discovery of Bookwyrm's fear and delight
fact: Grygum observed that Bookwyrm was both sincerely afraid something would happen to the adventurers and delighted to have them isolated and out of the way.
source_quote: I looked at her while she said it and found, underneath, that she meant the worry. It was real — she was sincerely afraid something would happen to us. Daz found the other half, the half I only saw land on his face: she was delighted to have us wrapped up and out of everything, no more heads poking anywhere.

subject: the final declaration of no trial
fact: Bookwyrm declared that today was not a day for trials and juries, and that the matter would be resolved after the naming by the new head of the Avowed.
source_quote: But today is not a day for trials and juries. That will be done after the naming, by the new head of the Avowed.

subject: the use of the Locate Object spell
fact: Grygum cast Locate Object to detect a sapphire on Bookwyrm, but found nothing, confirming she did not possess it.
source_quote: I reached out with the spell and found nothing where the sapphire should have been. Bookwyrm did not have it.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is referenced by Grygum as the ooze who consumed tea and the potion of flying, and who internally expressed approval of the flying skill, demonstrating a form of discipline and preference.
source_quote: Glabbagool was pleased with himself. *I like the flying skill,* he offered. *That was a good skill.*

subject: the group's decision to call Alkrist's accomplices
fact: The group chose to say only that there were accomplices in Janussi's death, avoiding direct accusation of Bookwyrm to maintain plausible deniability.
source_quote: Yeah — we know there are accomplices," I said.

subject: the final escort to chambers
fact: After being held in Deneir's Sanctum, the adventurers were to be escorted to their chambers later that evening, under Kalan's supervision.
source_quote: I will now ask Kalan Strongbranch to escort you to Deneir's Sanctum. ... where you will wait until later this evening, then be escorted to your chambers.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who could have cast lesser restoration but chose to hold his tongue, and who later observes Dawnbringer's demeanor opening up as if it were alive to praise.
source_quote: I could have done it myself. Lesser restoration is cheap and I had it to spend — I can always cast another on people, if we don't want to die, and Daral wasn't going to die. But a man shouldn't sit in his own rot while four strangers debate his usefulness. So I held my tongue and let the room work it out, because it was working itself toward mercy, which is the only direction I ever need it to go.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who was targeted by helmed horrors, later discovers the key in his pocket is the true object of their attack, and casts Scorching Ray to damage them.
source_quote: Behind us Daral was coming apart, saying it wasn't possible, these creatures can't be here, how could they. Fembris just stood in shock. I clocked both of them and put them out of my head. Panicking men are terrain you can't use. ... Daz went hunting through his spells and landed on the wrong idea first — something about breaking their minds — before the truth caught up. ... Daz passed the key to Grygum and threw the last of what he had at the one he'd been burning — three darts of light, all home.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the one who commands Dawnbringer to attack, uses her to land a stabilizing strike called 'sap', spends a trick to correct a misaligned swing, and later proposes using a dead helmed horror as a divining rod to detect who else possesses the key.
source_quote: Alright — let's go ahead and attack. With Dawnbringer." I brought her around and caught the one closest to me clean — a real bite, staggering it. Then the sword did its thing: the horror's movements went slow and sloppy, off-balance for its next swing. Sap, I call it. "This is good — let's do it again." When my follow-up nearly slid wide, I spent one of the tricks I keep in my back pocket and dragged the strike back on line. ... "Can we grab one of them and use it to detect who else has the key?" I said. "Turn it into a sort of divining rod, as it were.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the one who identifies the helmed horrors as animated armor, attempts to speak to them, grapples one, and uses Glabbagool's acid to dissolve its armor, later deduces the horrors were tracking the key, not the bearer.
source_quote: Seems like it's a helmed horror?" Zalthir said. He was already reading it. "Is this, like, animated armor or something?" ... Zalthir tried "Hello?" on it, the way you'd try a locked door. It didn't answer. It hit him — steel, and something colder behind the steel — and he shrugged most of it off. ... Zalthir finished the one clamped in his grip — a heavy punch, and Glabbagool's last mouthful of acid to go with it. ... Zalthir was already working it backward. When Grygum handed the key to Daz — who saw it? Fembris. Standing right there with the four of us.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum casts a burst of clean light that affects two helmed horrors, assures Daz he has healing and Revivify spells ready, receives the key from Daz, and later says, 'Don't you worry, Daz. You're going to be fine. Totally fine.'
source_quote: Grygum stepped up and let go a burst of clean light that caught two of them at once, both flinching under it. ... 'Don't worry, I've got plenty of heal spells, buddy. If you get knocked out, I'll just heal you — you'll be back up in no time.' A beat later: 'I also have Revivify, so we're covered either way.' ... Grygum handed the key to Daz

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who holds the inert key that triggers the helmed horrors' attack, survives being targeted by them, and after the battle, is assured by Grygum he will be fine.
source_quote: Behind us Daral was coming apart, saying it wasn't possible, these creatures can't be here, how could they. ... Daz passed the key to Grygum and threw the last of what he had at the one he'd been burning — three darts of light, all home. ... 'Ouch,' Daz said. 'I may drink a healing.' ... 'Don't you worry, Daz. You're going to be fine. Totally fine.'

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is the location where Grygum waits before the ambush, where the party sits after the battle, and where the locked door prevents escape even after Daral is healed.
source_quote: Waiting in Deneir's Sanctum ... So we sat in Deneir's office, fed by proxy, our patient healed, wondering how the story was going to end.

subject: Ambush of the Helmed Horrors
fact: The ambush of the Helmed Horrors occurs in Deneir's Sanctum, where glass and wood enter from three directions, and helmed horrors hover a hand's width off the floor, their eyes glowing with points of light.
source_quote: Glass and wood came in at the same time, from three directions, and for a breath none of us had moved. ... Suits of plate with nobody inside, walking and — this was the part that made my neck itch — hovering, lifting a hand's width off the floor and drifting. Little points of light where eyes should be.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sword that responds to Thorin's command, slows the movement of helmed horrors with 'sap', and is described as beautiful and worthy of study by Daral after being used to restore him.
source_quote: Dawnbringer, do your thing." ... The blade lit, poured into Daral, and took the sickness with it. ... "I shall do all kinds of new research on magical swords," he announced, "with the sentience and the beauty of Dawnbringer. I intend to make it an area of active research." ... I watched the whole demeanor of the thing open up, and I thought, *there it is, a small good thing in a room full of guards.*

subject: The Inert Key
fact: The Inert Key is a physical object carried by Daz that emits no magical signature but is the sole target of the helmed horrors, and is later used to deduce the assassins' objective.
source_quote: A key that read as nothing under every spell we'd thrown at it. Dead. Inert. And three suits of murderous plate had come through the windows to die for it. ... They weren't following a face. They were following the key itself, sniffing it out through plate and pocket both.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a creature riding Zalthir's arm that uses acid to dissolve helmed horror armor, consuming a piece of plate clean off during combat.
source_quote: Glabbagool — riding his arm — did the acid trick. Plate hissed and ran. Their armor was good, real good, and Glabbagool ate a piece of it clean off.

subject: Helmed Horror
fact: Helmed Horrors are animated suits of plate armor with no occupants, capable of hovering a hand's width above the ground, emitting glowing points of light where eyes should be, and attacking with single-minded purpose to retrieve the inert key.
source_quote: Suits of plate with nobody inside, walking and — this was the part that made my neck itch — hovering, lifting a hand's width off the floor and drifting. Little points of light where eyes should be. ... They're like AIs," I said. Closest real-world frame I had. A thing built to do one thing, that would do it until you stopped it, and no amount of talking would move it off. ... The armored hand closed on nothing. Daz slipped it — barely, the kind of even you only call a win because the other guy didn't get you.

subject: Dawnbringer's Restoration of Daral
fact: Dawnbringer is used to restore Daral from sickness, causing him to straighten, breathe, and become ecstatic, which triggers his sudden scholarly obsession with the sword's sentience and beauty.
source_quote: The blade lit, poured into Daral, and took the sickness with it. He straightened. He breathed. In the space of a heartbeat he was a well man, and he was ecstatic. ... 'I shall do all kinds of new research on magical swords,' he announced, 'with the sentience and the beauty of Dawnbringer. I intend to make it an area of active research.'

subject: The Helmed Horrors' Ambush
fact: Three helmed horrors enter Deneir's Sanctum through broken glass and wood, target Daz for the key in his pocket, attack Grygum after the key is transferred, and are ultimately destroyed one by one through fire, acid, and physical strikes.
source_quote: Glass and wood came in at the same time, from three directions, and for a breath none of us had moved. ... The first one went straight for Daz. ... The third one shoved past Grygum like he wasn't there and reached for Daz's throat. ... The horror on Daz landed one square. ... The horror on Grygum reached, missing, reaching, missing — Grygum kept his feet like the floor was the one thing he wasn't giving up. ... The suit came apart where it stood, and the last of them folded down into piles of rust and loose plate.

subject: The Discovery of the Key's Purpose
fact: After the battle, the party deduces that the helmed horrors were not targeting individuals but were drawn exclusively to the inert key, which emitted no magical signature but was the sole object of their aggression.
source_quote: They weren't following a face. They were following the key itself, sniffing it out through plate and pocket both. ... The reason you picked helmed horrors as assassins is they can't talk. Literally.

subject: Thorin's Proposal to Use a Dead Horror as a Divining Rod
fact: After the battle, Thorin proposes repurposing a destroyed helmed horror as a magical divining tool to detect who else possesses the inert key, suggesting a novel application of the enemy's remains.
source_quote: Can we grab one of them and use it to detect who else has the key?" I said. "Turn it into a sort of divining rod, as it were.

subject: The Locked Door in Deneir's Sanctum
fact: After Daral is healed and the battle ends, the party discovers the door to Deneir's Sanctum remains locked, trapping them despite their victory and leaving them to wonder how the story will end.
source_quote: Then Daral, glowing and cured and full of research, rose to leave — and found the door still locked. He was not going anywhere. None of us were. So we sat in Deneir's office, fed by proxy, our patient healed, wondering how the story was going to end.
